name: Question 10
problem:
A nutritionist measured $5$ particular features, ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{5},$ for each client in a group under a specific diet. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix $X,$ where each row contains measurements for a particular client.
The singular values of $X$ are 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}=6,\,{\sigma }_{2}=3,\,{\sigma }_{3}=2,\,{\sigma }_{4}=1,\,{\sigma }_{5}=0.6.
$$

The nutritionist then converted the original observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ using the equation $Y=X{V}_{2},$ where ${V}_{2}$ is the $5\times 2$ matrix consisting of the first two principal components of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix $Y$ compared to the initial observation matrix $X?$
worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the matrix of principal components. Then, applying the change of variables

$$
Y=XV
$$

we can convert our observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ of (linearly) transformed observations such that

- the covariance matrix of $Y$ is diagonal (meaning that the new features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}$ are uncorrelated),

- the features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}$ are arranged in order of decreasing variance, and

- the squares of the singular values ${\sigma }_{1}^{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2},…,{\sigma }_{5}^{2}$ represent the variances in the respective features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}.$

Now, the total variance over all features is proportional to the sum of the squared singular values:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Total} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(6)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(0.6)^{2} \\  & =50.36\end{aligned}
$$

Since the nutritionist used only the first two principal components, the remaining variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Remaining} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(6)^{2}+(3)^{2} \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our required percentage can be computed as

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{Remaining}}{\text{Total}} & =\frac{45}{50.36} \\  & ≈0.894 \\  & =89.4%.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

A nutritionist measured 5 particular features, x1,x2,…,x5, for each client in a group under a specific diet. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix X, where each row contains measurements for a particular client. The singular values of X are σ1=6,σ2=3,σ3=2,σ4=1,σ5=0.6. The nutritionist then converted the original observation matrix X into a new matrix Y using the equation Y=XV2, where V2 is the 5×2 matrix consisting of the first two principal components of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix Y compared to the initial observation matrix X?

a
87.6%
b
91.7%
c
89.4%
d
84.9%

86.7%
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let V be the matrix of principal components. Then, applying the change of variables

Y=XV

we can convert our observation matrix X into a new matrix Y of (linearly) transformed observations such that

  • the covariance matrix of Y is diagonal (meaning that the new features y1,y2,…,y5 are uncorrelated),

  • the features y1,y2,…,y5 are arranged in order of decreasing variance, and

  • the squares of the singular values σ12,σ22,…,σ52 represent the variances in the respective features y1,y2,…,y5.

Now, the total variance over all features is proportional to the sum of the squared singular values:

Total∝∑i=15σi2=(6)2+(3)2+(2)2+(1)2+(0.6)2=50.36

Since the nutritionist used only the first two principal components, the remaining variance is

Remaining∝∑i=12σi2=(6)2+(3)2=45.

Therefore, our required percentage can be computed as

RemainingTotal=4550.36≈0.894=89.4%.
